title: Domain Event envelope
description: Machine-readable Domain Event envelope contract: stable metadata shared by persistent domain-event records (docs/architecture/events.md). Envelope baseline only: no enforced event taxonomy, no payload taxonomy, no persistence encoding, no ordering or provenance envelope. The canonical G2 mutation taxonomy (ADR-0021, events.md section 4.1) is listed as event_type examples: nine lifecycle types plus project.created, task.created, task.dependency_added.
$comment: Persisted-fact envelope, not RPC: the schema describes committed facts and contains no execution-request fields. Schema-valid JSON != authoritative event: a model/provider cannot mint domain history by matching this shape; only trusted validated application services commit Event Journal facts. SECRET values must not enter journal payloads (INV-008); JSON Schema cannot prove data classification from arbitrary strings, so no fake regex security is attempted here — enforcement is Policy/application responsibility. additionalProperties is intentionally permissive so future domain-specific event data can extend this baseline once taxonomy is decided. event_type stays an open string (no enum) so the envelope never becomes a closed registry; the examples array records the canonical G2 names without enforcing them. This schema selects no Event Journal serialization encoding and introduces no Event Sourcing. See docs/architecture/events.md for semantics.

event_type.description: Typed event identity as non-empty string. Open vocabulary (no enum): exact naming convention for future types remains open, but the canonical G2 mutation names in examples are stable. Typed Agent Bus names and provider-specific types must not be read in here.

schema_version.description: Event-record schema version. Distinct from application build version, IPC protocol version, and provider version. No upcasting or deprecation policy is defined here.

occurred_at.description: Serialized timestamp representation only. Clock source, precision, monotonic ordering, and generation origin remain open implementation items.

correlation_id.description: Identifier of the larger operation/workflow/execution chain this fact belongs to. Format remains open; correlation != causation.

causation_id.description: Identifier of the prior action/event/request that directly caused this fact. Format remains open; causation != correlation.
